video_title: I Am #1 in the World with this GAME BREAKING Deck 🌎🏆

He treats the Hogs as chip, not as a kill attempt.

The enemy right tower reads 1373 -> 311 across 1084-1090s and he calls "that's going to be tower down" (1086s).

t=994.7s (clock unknown): used as the anchor of a stacked defence while conceding chip — "Let's go for the cannon here. We're taking some damage, but then once again like it really doesn't matter if it's in the opposite lanes" (996-1001s).

t=963-970s (clock unknown): he states the ability's limitation and the combo that fixes it — "that one musketeer in the back will stay alive on one HP cuz the mighty miner of course didn't like actually damage it, but it's going to know that mighty miner log plus e-spirit leaves musky's on basically one HP".
lightning: t=848.8s onward (clock unknown): he refuses to Lightning the opponent's Elixir Collector all game because it is his only Three Musketeers answer — "I can't lightning that elixir collector now cuz then he'll just 3M in the back and I'll lose the game because the ice golem will distract the mighty miner for too long. This will help out on defense."

t=897-916s (clock unknown): he describes the strongest Three Musketeers line against a Lightning deck — "He can go for like the ice golem in the back, the e-barbs to back, and then like a 3M at the bridge... he's just making it impossible for us to lightning the 3M cuz it's going to get soaked up by like the ice golem, the e-barbs, but they're going to live on low HP and then he's going to have three full musketeers that I have to deal with, which is super hard."

t=1078-1084s (clock unknown): the opponent plays it at the bridge instead, which is the mistake that loses him the tower — "I thought he was going to 3M in the middle, not at the bridge" (1082-1084s).
elixir-collector: Opponent's card, not played by Ryley. Three separate pumps are tracked (t=848.8s at (16, 27), 888.9s at (1, 27), 926.9s at (12, 27); clock unknown) and a fourth around 979.0s.

t=845-856s (clock unknown): he deliberately lets every pump live because the counter-spell is committed elsewhere — "I can't lightning that elixir collector now cuz then he'll just 3M in the back and I'll lose the game... I have to let that pump go and I think that means this match he will have a stack of pumps on me and there's nothing that I can really do about that." By 977s he is "down three elixir collectors" and at 1042s "down six elixir right now after that pump", and he still wins.
ice-golem: Mentioned, not played by Ryley — the opponent's spell-blocker. He cites it twice as the reason he cannot answer their pushes cleanly: "the ice golem will distract the mighty miner for too long" (852-854s) and "He's going to 3M the bridge again. Maybe ice golem first to block the lightning" (1013-1015s).
elite-barbarians: Opponent's card (tracked at t=882.9s, 934.9s, 963.0s; clock unknown), answered with the centre Cannon plus Mighty Miner. He treats them as the thing that can punish an over-commitment — "And we have to mighty miner. I'm worried about the e-barbs though... Is he going to e-barbs? No, he doesn't. Okay, we're chilling" (1026-1030s).
royal-ghost: Opponent's card, and Ryley identifies it as the Evolution variant ("the evo ghost", 920-922s). His standing answer is the Mighty Miner plus an Electro Spirit reset — "we can go for the mighty miner on the evo ghost" (920-922s), "just e-spirit the ghost" (927s), "Mighty miner on the ghost" (1012s).
bandit: Opponent's card. Early on it costs him tower HP through lag — "Oh my god, I lagged a bit on my cannon. That bandit's going to dash on my tower" (835-838s) — and later he chooses to concede the chip rather than spend: "Let's let the bandit go. Let's let the musky go. And we're in a fine spot right now" (971-974s).

bullets: Piloted as a defensive cycle deck that wins on chip: across 279 seconds (video 815.8-1094.8s; the in-game clock OCR failed for this video, so all times are video seconds) Ryley plays Cannon nine times, Skeletons eleven times and Electro Spirit eight times, and commits offence only in four Royal Hogs sets at the right-hand bridge tile (873.9s, 924.9s, 945.9s, 1078.1s).

The deck's whole plan against a Three Musketeers pump deck is to hold Lightning: "I can't lightning that elixir collector now cuz then he'll just 3M in the back and I'll lose the game" (845-852s) and "Lightning is just really good against three musketeers in general" (885-891s). He concedes three Elixir Collectors and a six-elixir deficit to keep the spell available.

Defensive stack of choice is Cannon in the middle plus Skeletons plus Electro Spirit, with the Mighty Miner as the anti-tank and The Log as the finisher: "mighty miner log plus e-spirit leaves musky's on basically one HP" (968-970s). He states the deck can simply turtle — "I definitely do trust my defense guys on just defending the whole match, especially having like Evo baby dragon and stuff" (937-940s).

Two Lightnings decided the game: t=951.0s at (15, 19) behind a Royal Hogs set took the enemy right tower from 2734 to 1485 HP, and t=1020.0s at (14, 17) caught two more Musketeers. The final Royal Hogs set at 1078.1s finished the tower (1373 -> 311 HP across 1084-1090s) for the win — "There's no way that he can save this. Let's go. GG's" (1086-1088s).

new_deck.display_name: Royal Hogs Mighty Miner Lightning Cycle
new_deck.rationale: Average elixir 3.25 with a 7-elixir four-card cycle (Skeletons, Electro Spirit, The Log, Cannon) feeding a fast 5-elixir win condition thrown as a punish, but it defends first and chips second, which is why control is the secondary read.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The cheap defensive core — Cannon in the middle, Skeletons, Electro Spirit and The Log — answers bridge spam and swarm pushes for one to three elixir at a time, which lets the deck survive a large elixir deficit against pump decks. Mighty Miner covers the tanks and charge units that cheap cards cannot, and his Explosive Escape bomb plus Log plus Electro Spirit is a repeatable package that leaves ranged support on almost no hit points. Lightning is held as a single-purpose answer to Three Musketeers and to grouped support behind a push, and because the deck spends so little on defence it can afford the 6-elixir cast at the moment it lands on three targets. Royal Hogs is the only offence: four hogs at the bridge thrown on a read of a pump or a Musketeers commitment, deliberately as chip rather than as a kill attempt. In this match that combination — turtle, refuse to spend Lightning on pumps, punish with Hogs — beat a Three Musketeers Elixir Collector deck that was up six elixir for most of the game.
